entries.title: Caching strategies
entries.summary: Cache-aside, write-through and write-back trade freshness against latency and complexity.
body: Cache-aside: read from cache, fall back to the database, then populate the cache. Most common default.
Always pair a cache with an eviction policy such as LRU and a TTL for staleness.
tradeoffs: Stale reads are possible unless invalidation is handled on writes.
Cache stampedes can happen when a hot key expires; use request coalescing or jittered TTLs.

entries.title: URL shortener
entries.summary: Map a short code to a long URL with high read volume and simple writes.
requirements: Create short links, redirect on read, optional expiry.
components: API service behind a load balancer
Key-value store keyed by short code
Cache in front of the store for hot links
tradeoffs: Base62 counter-based IDs are simple and collision free; random IDs need a uniqueness check.
